To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a glide matching refrigerant can improve the exergy efficiency of a shell-and-tube heat exchanger by 5-15%, depending on the configuration and the superheat level.
the effect of temperature profile on the relative performance can be substantial.
the Modelica-based modelling and simulations of dry-expansion evaporators can be used to evaluate the performance of different heat exchanger configurations and refrigerant mixtures.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an advanced model of shell-and-tube heat exchanger working with alternative refrigerants and the simulation of the heat exchanger performance for different refrigerant mixtures, different heat exchanger configurations and different operating conditions.
the modelling of shell-and-tube dry-expansion evaporators using zeotropic mixtures as working fluids.
the modelling and simulation of shell-and-tube heat exchangers working with zeotropic refrigerant blends, and with the evaluation of their relative performance in different flow arrangements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the effect of the refrigerant mixture glide on the heat transfer is not significant for the evaporator, while the effect of the mixture glide on the total exergy loss is very significant.
a dry-expansion evaporator working with alternative refrigerants is a complex device and the performance of any configuration is very sensitive to the operating conditions.
the U-tube configuration with a glide matching refrigerant mixtures is more efficient compared to the standard counter-flow configuration with HFC-34a.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new methodology of modelling and simulation is a powerful tool for the analysis and optimization of the shell-and-tube heat exchangers working with alternative refrigerants mixtures.
the Modelica-based model is an accurate tool to simulate the performance of shell-and-tube heat exchangers working with alternative refrigerants.
the use of alternative refrigerant mixures can be beneficial in some cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a zeotropic mixture in an evaporator can be beneficial in terms of exergy efficiency and COP if a proper heat exchanger configuration is chosen.
the use of glide matching refrigerant mixtures can lead to substantial improvements of the performance of the evaporators.
the dry-expansion evaporator is a good candidate to work with alternative working fluids.
